info.name: OPEX + Arapoush website
info.description: Generated from the route contracts (`pnpm docs:api`); do not edit by hand. Choose an environment (local or staging). Console routes: run **Sign-in and sessions → Step 1** then **Step 2** (the CSRF token is stored for you). Partner routes need DPoP proofs and RFC 9421 signatures per request: use the PHP reference client, or fill {{dpopProof}}, {{signatureInput}} and {{signature}} yourself. Never put production credentials in an environment.

item.name: Import Arapoush size charts into the tube catalogue

header.description: Set automatically after the MFA sign-in request (or GET /v1/manage/auth/csrf).

request.description:
Reads one or more size charts (.xlsx, one cross-section per file) and applies them to the current draft of `product.tube.catalogue`: sizes and volumes per diameter, which closures fit, and the colour families each closure comes in. Closures are matched by id, Persian name or `aliases`; unknown ones are added with a warning. Without `apply` it only previews (the changes against the draft). With `apply` it saves a new draft revision, which is published the normal way.

Source: catalogue/routes.ts

item.name: Upload factory CAD (STEP/STP or GLB) for a closure

header.description: Set automatically after the MFA sign-in request (or GET /v1/manage/auth/csrf).

request.description:
Converts the file to an optimized GLB in millimetres (OpenCascade for STEP, glTF Transform for both) in a worker, stores it and returns the model for review with a mounting suggested from the geometry. Nothing reaches the website until an operator sets the mounting and approves it. With `shape` and `diameter` the model is used only at that diameter. Limits: 25 MB, 2,000,000 triangles before simplification, 90 s.

Source: catalogue/routes.ts

The previously approved model for the same place is archived. The website shows it after the draft is published; the parametric shape stays as the fallback.

item.name: Submit a form (becomes a helpdesk ticket)

header.description: The visitor's IP (per-IP limit, audit).

request.description:
Sent by the website's server (/api/forms/{slug}) with the visitor's IP in `X-End-User-IP`. Answers are validated against the published definition: unknown fields are refused and fields hidden by a condition are dropped. Files travel base64 in `files` (max 10 MB each, 5 in all, kinds allowed by the field, virus-scanned). Personal data is stored encrypted; the audit log never holds it. A sender blocked as spam gets 202 and nothing is stored. The P8 body shape (`subject`, `spec`, `fields`) is still accepted.

Source: forms/routes.ts

header.description: DPoP proof for POST to this URL.

request.description:
Client authentication is private_key_jwt only (`client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer`, ES256, aud = this URL, single-use jti). Every request needs a `DPoP` proof header; tokens are bound to that key. Errors follow RFC 6749 (`error`, `error_description`), not problem+json.

item.name: A visitor sends a form (the browser posts here; the server forwards to OPEX)

request.description:
Adds the visitor's IP and the delivery token, so OPEX credentials never reach the browser. Bot checks here: a filled honeypot (`website`) or a form sent faster than 2.5 s after it was shown (or older than a day) gets 202 and is dropped. Body limit 16 MB (files are base64).

Source: apps/web/app/api/forms/[form]/route.ts

item.name: Open a draft preview (link from the OPEX console or a partner preview)

request.description:
Stores the signed token in an HttpOnly cookie (`opex_preview`, 30 minutes; SameSite=None over https so it works inside the console frame), turns on draft mode and redirects to `path`. With `edit=1` the visual editor's bridge loads too (`opex_edit` cookie). `exit=1` leaves preview.

Source: apps/web/app/api/opex/preview/route.ts

item.name: Webhook receiver: OPEX published something; refresh the pages

header.description: t=<unix>, v1=<hex HMAC>

request.description:
Verifies `OPEX-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 with OPEX_WEBHOOK_SECRET over `t.body`, 5-minute window) and refuses a repeated event id, then revalidates the `opex` cache tag.

Source: apps/web/app/api/opex/revalidate/route.ts
